flows, a stronger do-not-contact list, teams and outbound queues on every call, missed-call search, and copying messaging settings between accounts.

Conversation flows: chat, WhatsApp, SMS and other messaging channels can now be run by a flow, built in the flow designer the same way as a call flow. A flow can ask questions, offer options (numbered where a channel has no buttons, such as SMS and email), and hand the customer to people. A customer who replies with one of the hand-over words is handed to people at once, wherever they are in the flow.

Do-not-contact upgrade: the list now covers more than numbers on a page. Every block says which channels it applies to and why, and a customer's STOP from a marketing message stops marketing unless you choose everything. Existing blocks keep blocking every channel, as before. New: scrub reports, a check that other systems can call, a customer preference page, consent that expires and can be asked for again, number ranges, lists of known litigators, a reassigned-number check (needs a provider account), an export for the regulator, and an alert when someone tries to contact a blocked customer. STOP words are understood in more languages. The SA National Opt-Out Register is available but stays off until its source is set.

Calls and teams: every call now carries a team, so call reports and drill-downs follow the team that took the call. A queue can also have a Reporting team: its calls are counted under that team in reports, without changing who can take them, and "Apply to past calls" brings older calls in line. Agents can pick the outbound queue they are dialling for, each queue says whether outbound calls are allowed from it, and a new search finds missed calls.

Copy messaging settings: hand-over messages, opening hours and automatic answers can be copied from another account instead of being typed again.

Fixes: a name changed under Users now updates the name shown at sign-in."}
